focus: CI workflow pass: read every uncited .github/workflows file, record trigger, SKILLED_CI switch, scripts and whether each resolves; find a step that cannot fail, a switch a workflow ignores, and a suite on disk that no workflow runs

label: Four tracked sk-git test suites are run by no workflow: commit-id-naming.test.sh, stamp-branch.test.sh, migrate-legacy-branch-names.test.sh and validate-message-git-timeout.test.mjs. The workflow named 'sk-git script tests' runs only worktree-naming.test.sh, and the doctor suite git-hook-gates.test.cjs mentions none of the four, so a regression in branch stamping, commit-id allocation or the bounded-git gate ships green.

The trigger-index rebuild commit carries [skip ci], which suppresses every push-triggered workflow for that commit including message-contract.yml, the only status context the branch ruleset requires. The workflows README and the /doctor:ci toggle both treat 'a skipped job reports Success' as the reason the message contract must never be switched off, yet the repository's own bot produces that state on every rebuild and no document names the exception.

The v4.0.0.16 note says the repository's 33 workflows used about 3,812 runner-minutes a day; the repository has 32 workflow files and the doctor CI report also counts 32, so the baseline set the cost claims rest on cannot be reconstructed from the tree.

ci-report returned zero flags across all 32 workflows while four tracked suites were unreferenced, because all eight flags test a single workflow file in isolation and none crosses from a run: line to the tree. A ninth suite-unwired flag built from the profile's source roots would catch it with no new field.

The job named 'sk-git script tests' runs one suite named 'Run the worktree-naming suite', so a green context asserts coverage the job does not have; an absent check invites inspection and a misnamed green one does not.
A workflow-named script path must resolve on disk. All 32 named paths resolve in both source roots, so the CI script inventory is sound and the F18-01 class is wiring, not missing files.

direction: A step in .github/workflows that cannot fail
reason: Every continue-on-error and exit 0 site was read in context: advisory-checks.yml's three are advisory by design with the reason beside them, strict-pass-freshness-report.yml's is on a repair step, and the four exit 0 sites are skip or no-op branches. No '|| true' is attached to any checker invocation in .github/workflows.

direction: A SKILLED_CI switch that a workflow ignores or a group the README table misstates
reason: The README's five group rows match the code exactly: 8 FRESHNESS, 17 TESTS, 3 REVIEW, 2 REPORTS, 1 MESSAGES, plus the profile's exempt dependabot-auto-merge.yml. ci-report found 0 flags and errors []. .env.example documents no SKILLED_CI name, so no switch is documented and unread.

direction: A protected workflow switched off without extra friction
reason: trigger-index-rebuild.yml is protected and sits under SKILLED_CI_REPORTS, which the README invites turning off, but doctor-ci-toggle.yaml requires a second named confirmation for a protected workflow. Designed behaviour, not a bypass.

direction: Duplicate doctor runners caused by a symlinked .opencode/commands
reason: .opencode/commands is a real directory, not a symlink, and both doctor test trees resolve, so the .opencode and .skilled runner references are not two names for one file.
